title.rendered: Do You Not Perceive It? — Morning Devotional

excerpt.rendered: God says “I am doing a new thing” — present tense, right now, in the middle of your wilderness. A post-Easter devotional on letting go of the past and perceiving what God is already building.

content.rendered:
Gospelbuzz Morning Devotional — Tuesday, April 7, 2026

Scripture for Today — Isaiah 43:18–19

“Forget the former things; do not dwell on the past. See, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it? I am making a way in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland.”
— Isaiah 43:18–19 (NIV)

Today’s Devotional Message

One week ago today, Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey while the crowd cheered. Four days later He was dead. Three days after that He was risen. And now — seven days on — the world is fundamentally different, even though most of it doesn’t know it yet.

That is the nature of new things. They begin before they are visible. They are real before they are recognised.

Isaiah 43 was written to a people in exile — a community that had lost everything, carried off to Babylon, grieving what had been. God’s word to them was not a historical commentary. It was a disruption. Stop looking back. Something new is happening. Look forward. Do you not see it?

The remarkable thing about this verse is not just the promise of a new thing — it is the tense. I am doing. Present continuous. Not “I will eventually do” or “I did once before.” Right now, in the middle of the exile, in the middle of the wasteland, in the middle of the grief — God is already at work. The way through the wilderness is already being made. The streams in the desert are already being opened. The new thing is already underway.

The question God asks is not rhetorical. It is a genuine invitation: do you not perceive it? Are you paying attention? Or are you so locked into mourning what was lost that you are missing what is being born?

Post-Easter, this word lands with particular force. The resurrection was the ultimate new thing — the pivot point of all history. But it did not end there. The risen Jesus is still making new things. He is still opening ways through impossible places, still causing streams to flow in the dry and dusty seasons of ordinary human lives.

What “former thing” are you still dwelling on today? What past loss or failure or missed opportunity still has more of your attention than the new thing God is doing right now? Easter is the permission to let it go — to turn from the tomb and walk into the morning.

The new thing is already springing up. Do you perceive it?

Prayer for Today

Lord, forgive me for living in the rear-view mirror. I confess that I sometimes hold onto the pain of the past more tightly than I hold onto the promises of the future. Today I choose to turn around — to look forward, not backward. Show me the new thing You are doing in my life right now. Open my eyes to see the way You are making in the wilderness. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Daily Declaration

“God is doing a new thing in my life — right now, today. I let go of the former things. I stop dwelling on the past. I open my eyes to see the way He is making in my wilderness. Streams are flowing in my desert. I perceive it by faith.”

📖 Further Reading — Related Scriptures

  • Isaiah 40:31 — “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength.” — The promise of renewal for those who keep looking forward.
  • Lamentations 3:22–23 — “His mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning.” — Every day is a fresh beginning with God.
  • 2 Corinthians 5:17 — “If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: the old has gone, the new is here!” — The theological foundation of every new beginning.
  • Philippians 3:13–14 — “Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead, I press on toward the goal.” — Paul’s personal practice of forward-looking faith.
  • Revelation 21:5 — “He who was seated on the throne said, ‘I am making everything new!'” — The ultimate promise: God is in the business of new beginnings.
